A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TetHeart study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including v2 Appendices A–G and v3 Appendices A–I. Reformatting and renumbering can be matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original cardiac reconstruction experiments, clinical-index estimates, external evaluations and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds quantitative iCMR evaluation, strain analysis, robustness experiments and further ablations.

M1.justification: The default architecture and losses remain unchanged. Appendix F introduces an exploratory template-initialized variant using positional queries instead of image-based queries and removing static–motion feature concatenation (Table 14). This explicitly changes the procedure for that probe; the added AFA pseudocode primarily documents the existing method.

E1.justification: ACDC, M&Ms, M&Ms-2, iCMR and 4DM remain the datasets used. V3 adds simulated interventional corruption conditions and a generic-template initialization scenario. Quantitative iCMR and strain reporting extend evaluation of retained data rather than introducing new datasets or populations.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds MulViMotion and DeepMesh to both sparse-input comparisons; v2 evaluated them only with full stacks. Appendix C explains their zero-padding adaptation. V3 also introduces an iCMR comparison against 4DMR, MR-Net, Ours-Mesh and Ours-SDF, where v2 presented only TetHeart visualizations.

E3.justification: V3 adds corrupted-ES testing with downsampling, noise and 10-degree rotation, quantitative iCMR Dice evaluation, ED-to-ES strain MAE, and training, initialization and refinement controls. The existing 835-sequence split ratio, resampling and training budgets remain unchanged. Subject-level splitting and training augmentation are newly documented, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test augmentation under artifacts, full-stack-only training, pretrained initialization versus weight sharing, refinement iteration counts and generic-template initialization. Appendix D adds strain validation; Appendix F adds an image-quality comparison and a myocardial-infarction failure case. Existing AFA-configuration, slice-position and category-wise ablations are retained.

E5.justification: V3 introduces paired t-tests for baseline comparisons, external evaluation and ablations, including nonsignificant full-stack representation comparisons. Figure 5 adds shaded bands without defining their statistical meaning. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds. The new iCMR significance paragraph names Chamfer Distance although Table 4 reports Dice.

E6.justification: V3 adds baseline, robustness and probe results, including iCMR Dice scores of 80.15/83.22/79.76% for TetHeart's myocardium/LV/RV and GLS MAE of 2.18%. Existing TetHeart benchmark and 4DM scores remain unchanged. In Table 3, MulViMotion myocardium Dice changes from 72.30 to 75.31% on M&Ms and from 68.21 to 75.23% on M&Ms-2 under the retained full-stack setting.

T1.justification: The tetrahedral representation, attention formulation, vertex-update equations, losses and Appendix A.3 metric formulas remain mathematically equivalent. Algorithm 1 explains the existing AFA procedure. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a unified end-to-end framework spanning full-stack to single-slice reconstruction, using attentive assembly, distillation and keyframe supervision. State-of-the-art performance and external evaluation without retraining remain central claims. Removing 'zero-shot' and softening generalization wording do not materially change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies the weight-sharing explanation through a pretrained, unshared control with comparable accuracy, and discusses initialization priors, refinement limits and failure-case volume errors. New limitations address distillation-induced averaged or hallucinated anatomy, missed pathology and clinician oversight. It also removes v2's explicit statement that iCMR evaluation can only be qualitative.

D1.justification: V3 substantially expands reproducibility documentation with AFA pseudocode, augmentation operations, subject-level split disclosure, baseline zero-padding details and model parameter counts. Its abstract supplies a code/data link, and Appendix G gives video access instructions; v2 only promised public code. Existing optimizer, epoch and hardware specifications are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds Götte et al. (2025) on MR-guided ventricular ablation and expands the clinical-adoption motivation. The principal related-work coverage and positioning remain intact. Switching to author–year citations and updating bibliographic details do not constitute additional research-positioning changes.

P1.justification: V3 copyedits retained prose, adds 'Mesh' to the printed title, revises author information, merges contribution bullets and expands training explanations. It adds visualization-access and broader-impact sections while retaining the main section order and much of the original narrative.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column conference formatting to a single-column journal layout, with extensive display resizing and relocation. V3 adds hospital photographs, AFA pseudocode, a training diagram, new tables and diagnostic figures, and shaded bands in Figure 5. Duplicate supplementary visualizations are consolidated into enlarged main-text figures.

improvement.justification: Additional sparse-input baselines, artifact tests, strain validation and initialization controls strengthen the evidence, while the failure case and hallucination discussion better qualify clinical applicability. These improve v2's existing empirical foundation. Gains are limited by undefined Figure 5 bands and the new iCMR evaluation's unclear reference-annotation protocol and Dice/Chamfer-Distance mismatch in Appendix D.
